list: The official 55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze. Names, descriptions and grades as PlayStation publishes them, via Exophase and PSNProfiles (2026-11-18). Guides, roadmap stages and missable verdicts are this guide's own work, reasoned from the official descriptions.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.missableNote: The platinum itself cannot be missed, but it inherits every missable below: clear the Likely and Possible trophies on your story run and it needs no second playthrough.
trophies.guide: The platinum, awarded the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned. Treat this guide as the order of work: play the story once with the missable warnings in view, then sweep collectibles, then grind the activity and money totals, and finish with A Long Road (100% completion), which by definition is the last long pole.
steps: Follow the five roadmap stages in order; do not leave the story until every Likely/Possible trophy tied to it is done.
Keep a manual save before each chapter ends so a missed one-off can be recovered without a new game.
After the credits, sweep Stage 3 collectibles, then Stage 4 activities and economy totals.
Close out A Long Road (100%) and this platinum unlocks with it.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.missableNote: Gone Fishing is a single named mission. The description does not promise a replay, so finish it when the story offers it rather than assuming you can return.
trophies.guide: Finish Gone Fishing, the mission the game opens with. Play it straight through to its end marker; nothing in the description asks for a score, a time or a clean run, so a plain completion is the whole requirement. If you are ever offered a chance to skip ahead, decline until this is banked.
steps: Start the story and accept Gone Fishing when it is offered.
Follow the mission objectives to the final marker without quitting to free roam mid-mission.
Let the completion banner play out; the trophy should pop as the mission closes.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.missableNote: Not missable by itself, but 100% completion sweeps in side strands and one-off content that can be locked by story choices, so it inherits their risk. PlayStation tracks this as a percentage; the target is the full 100.
trophies.guide: Attain 100% completion, the second gold and the natural finale of the platinum run. The game's own completion checklist is the authority here: story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and discoveries all feed it. Work this guide's stages in order and check the in-game percentage as you go; when everything else on this page is ticked, the last few percent are usually a strand or an activity type you only tried once.
steps: Finish the story and all eight-plus stranger strands.
Complete every collectible set and discovery count in Stage 3.
Try every activity type (Master of None) and finish the Stage 4 mastery totals.
Use the in-game stats screen to hunt the final missing percent.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.missableNote: Stunt locations are fixed world content and stay available after the story; this is a volume grind, not a risk.
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts, a silver and the biggest single count on the list. Stunts are the marked jumps and set-piece leaps scattered over Leonida; each one completed counts, and PlayStation tracks the total, so the counter in this app mirrors the game's. Work region by region, take a fast car or bike to each marker, and save the awkward multi-part jumps for last, when your driving is warmed up.
steps: Unlock the full map through the story first; stunt markers are everywhere.
Sweep one region at a time and tick each stunt in this app as it lands.
Use a durable, fast vehicle; a failed landing costs seconds, not progress.
Check your running total against the 250 target in the stats screen.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.missableNote: Activity types stay on the map after the story; you can sample the last missing type at any time.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once. The list of types is the game's activity menu: races, drone races, fishing, arcade games, shooting ranges, stunts, bowling, meditation and the rest as they unlock. You do not need to win or even finish most of them — one genuine attempt at each type is what the description asks. This trophy doubles as a tour that shows you where every other activity trophy lives, so do it early in Stage 4.
steps: Open the map or activity menu and note every activity icon type.
Play one session of each type, win or lose.
If the trophy has not popped, a type is still locked behind story progress; return after the credits.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.missableNote: Rated Possible out of caution: the description does not confirm the ranges stay open forever. In practice ranges are repeatable, so the real risk is leaving all 42 golds to the very end of a long grind.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — PlayStation tracks 42 of them, and this silver is the list's main test of raw skill. Learn each range's target pattern at bronze pace first, then chase gold once the rhythm is familiar; medals are per challenge, so bank them one range at a time and keep your counter here in step with the game. If a weapon class feels weak, its challenges are the ones to repeat, not the ones you already golded.
steps: Visit every Shooting Range and run each challenge once to learn its pattern.
Replay challenges in place until each shows a gold medal; tick them off here as you go.
Save the highest-score challenges for last, when your aim settings are dialled in.
Stop at 42 of 42 golds; the trophy pops on the final medal.

Learn a course with a practice run, then race it for the win while the line is fresh; drone handling rewards smooth, early turns over raw speed.
steps: Note every Top Fun location as it appears on your map.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.missableNote: Races are repeatable map content; a loss costs nothing and every race can be re-run until won.
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word that matters is different: repeating your favourite circuit twenty times earns nothing, so keep a list — the counter in this app — and move to a fresh event after each win. Any race type should count toward the twenty, so mix road races with the drone events you are winning anyway for Top Fun and let the two trophies feed each other.
steps: Enter a race, win it, and tick it off here before entering another.
Always pick an event you have not already won; variety is the requirement.
If a race is too hot, leave it and bank an easier win elsewhere; come back with a better vehicle.
The trophy pops on your twentieth distinct win.

Play it through to its completion state, not just a game over.

Each works the same way: a named character offers a chain of missions outside the main chapters, and the trophy is for the last one. The habit that earns all five is simple — never leave a character's newest mission sitting while you push the main story, because strands are cheapest to finish while their giver is still around.

Follow his chain to the mission the game marks as his final one.
Complete it and confirm the trophy before moving on.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: The list's clearest missable. Stranger strands are optional, scattered, and in this series they routinely close as chapters pass or choices land; a strand you never start can be gone for the run. Eight are needed and there may not be many more than eight.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida, a silver and the trophy this guide most wants you to fear. A strand is a stranger's whole little storyline, not a single mission, and the five character finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are exactly this kind of content. Start every stranger you meet the moment you meet them, finish strands before pushing chapters, and count completions here against the eight PlayStation tracks. If you finish the story short of eight, sweep the map for question-mark strangers before assuming the run is lost — but do not count on it.
steps: From Chapter 1 on, stop for every stranger marker and start the strand.
Finish each strand promptly; do not stack up half-done strands across chapters.
Tick each completed strand here and check the count against the target of 8.
If you reach the endgame short, sweep region by region for any strand still open.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableNote: Your partner is a standing mechanic and wanted levels can be manufactured at will; this can be engineered on any free-roam session.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. This is an engineered trophy, not a lucky one: with your partner beside you, commit enough crime in one place to reach exactly the four-star neighbourhood, then break line of sight and hide until the stars drain. The description's care is in the wording — with your partner — so both characters need to be present and free when the level clears, not one of them busted or wasted mid-escape.
steps: Free-roam with your partner and raise your Wanted Level to 4 stars in a vehicle you can escape in.
Break police line of sight: tunnels, alleys, rooftops and vehicle swaps all serve.
Stay hidden with your partner until the Wanted Level fully clears.
